newsitem.title: USA: Central Hudson starts NY 600 MW power unit.
newsitem.headline: Central Hudson starts NY 600 MW power unit.

text.p: Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp said Tuesday it restarted a 600 megawatt (MW) unit at its Roseton generating facility.

The utility switched on the unit, in Newburgh, N.Y., at the request of the New York Power Pool (NYPP), the group that oversees transmission reliability of the state's electric grid, company spokesman Peter Burdash said.
It was not necessary to fire up a second 600 MW unit at the Roseton site, which burns either fuel oil or natural gas, given projected power demand, he added.
NYPP request aimed at ensuring transmission stability in the southeastern portion of the power grid during a five-day maintenance outage of a 345 kilovolt (KV) transmission line.

The shutdown of the high-voltage line, which began Monday, cut power transfer capability at the so-called Central-East Interface by 1,000 megawatts (MW). The normal limit on the interface is 2,600-2,700 MW.
